title: Let the catalog preview bot run against already-open PRs
body:
Adds a `workflow_dispatch` mode to the catalog preview so it can be run against PRs that are already open (`pull_request_target` only fires on new activity). Takes a PR number or `all`, with a dry run option that renders without posting.

Dry-run locally across all 63 open PRs: 61 render, 2 correctly skipped (#282 and #283 change only the schema), 0 failures. Largest is #231 at 770 entries, which truncates at 668 with a note saying so.

Needs merging before the sweep can be run, since `workflow_dispatch` only works from the default branch.

title: Allow fixed names for single-color filaments
body:
Single-color products such as eMarble currently need a `{color_name}` placeholder even when the product name is already complete. Allow a fixed name when `colors` contains exactly one entry; keep the placeholder mandatory for multiple color entries so their compiled names remain distinct.

Updates the schema, linter and contributor documentation. The compiler already supports fixed names. Adds six regression cases covering fixed and templated names, multiple colors, invalid placeholders, empty names, and expansion across weights and diameters, and runs them in CI.

Closes #63.

Validation:
- New filament-name regression checks and existing catalog-preview checks pass.
- All material and filament source files pass schema validation.
- Full catalog compilation succeeds; generated output is byte-for-byte identical to main.
- Full-catalog lint results are unchanged: 128 pre-existing errors and 262 warnings across 86 files.
- Diff whitespace check passes with the existing CRLF schema line endings preserved.

title: Add per-color transmission distance to filament data
body:
Closes #295.

Add optional `transmission_distance` to each color in the filament source schema. Values are positive numbers in millimeters and are passed through to the compiled database; colors without a known value produce `null`, following the existing optional-field convention.

[HueForge describes TD](https://shop.thehueforge.com/blogs/news/what-is-hueforge) as light penetration through a thickness of material, affected by pigments. Store it per color and apply it to every listed weight and diameter. No diameter restriction is needed solely because the feedstock diameter differs. If diameter variants have different measured TD values, contributors can split them into separate filament objects, as documented in the README.

Validation:
- Validated all 86 manufacturer files and materials against their schemas.
- Checked that the TD schema accepts omitted and positive values, and rejects zero, negative, null and non-numeric values.
- Added a compilation self-check to CI covering distinct color values, missing values, weight/diameter expansion and diameter-specific values in separate objects; it passes on Python 3.11.
- Existing catalog preview tests and the full database build pass.
- Compared all 9,427 compiled entries against the previous compiler: existing fields and IDs are unchanged; the only addition is `transmission_distance: null`.

This adds field support only; no manufacturer TD values are populated.

title: feat: preserve filament country of origin
body:
## Summary

- allow an optional `country_of_origin` field in filament source data
- preserve the manufacturing country in compiled database output
- add a regression test and run it in CI

## Why

This extracts country-of-origin metadata from the former large PR #277 into a focused change. The field describes where the filament was manufactured, not merely where the brand is based.

## Validation

- `python -m json.tool filaments.schema.json`
- `python -m check_jsonschema --schemafile filaments.schema.json filaments\\*.json`
- `python -m unittest discover -s tests -v`
- `python scripts\\compile_filaments.py`
- `git -c core.whitespace=cr-at-eol diff --check`

Supersedes the country-of-origin metadata portion of #277.

title: feat(data): add Inslogic filaments
body:
## Summary

Adds five current Inslogic filament families, covering 39 compiled color variants:

- PLA Pro (12 colors)
- Matte PLA (7 colors)
- PETG Pro (11 colors)
- High-Speed PLA Pro (7 colors)
- ASA (2 colors)

This data was extracted from an independently maintained Community dataset, then revalidated against current first-party Inslogic product pages and technical documentation before being adapted to the present Donkie/SpoolmanDB schema.

Fixes #296.

## Official sources

- [Inslogic filament catalog](https://store.inslogic3d.com/collections/filament)
- [PLA Pro](https://store.inslogic3d.com/products/pla-pro-filament)
- [Matte PLA](https://store.inslogic3d.com/products/matte-pla-filament)
- [PETG Pro](https://store.inslogic3d.com/products/petg-pro-filament)
- [PETG Pro TDS](https://cdn.shopify.com/s/files/1/0822/8611/7163/files/Inslogic_PETG_Pro_Filament_Technical_Data_Sheet_TDS.pdf?v=1739875791)
- [High-Speed PLA Pro](https://store.inslogic3d.com/products/high-speed-pla-pro-filament)
- [ASA](https://store.inslogic3d.com/products/asa-filament)

## Deliberate omissions

- Refill variants are omitted because the current schema has no explicit refill semantic and the spooled/refill offerings can share the same net weight.
- `spool_type` is omitted because the current reusable spool is a composite of reusable plastic sides and a cardboard coil; a single material enum would be ambiguous. The manufacturer-published combined tare is retained as `spool_weight`.
- Product URLs, TDS/SDS URLs, SKUs/codes, EANs, and country of origin are omitted because the current upstream schema does not support them.
- The wider engineering and aesthetic catalog is left for later focused, first-party-verified batches rather than importing older Community values wholesale.

No schema or compiler changes are included, and no unsupported Community extensions are present.

## Validation

- Validated `materials.json` and all 54 filament source files against the current upstream JSON schemas using `jsonschema`.
- Ran `python scripts/compile_filaments.py` successfully.
- Confirmed exactly 39 new Inslogic compiled records with unique generated IDs.
- Ran `git diff --check` successfully.

title: Sunlu: add PETG 2.0 (20 colors)
body:
Adds Sunlu's PETG 2.0 line: 20 colors, 1 kg, 1.75 mm, plastic spool.

## Sources

- **What's sold** (colors, 1 kg / 1.75 mm only): [Sunlu store, PETG 2.0](https://store.sunlu.com/products/petg-v2-3d-printer-filament-1kg)
- **Density, temperatures, hex codes:** [Sunlu PETG 2.0 product page](https://www.sunlu.com/products/PETG2.0). The "Parameter Information" and "Color Code" tables
- **Density cross-check:** [Sunlu PETG 2.0 TDS](https://media.sunlu.com/prod/20260916/30522971789539747056.pdf?filename=TDS), doc SL-TE-WI-164 rev A/0. 1.22 g/cm³, ISO 1183

The official product page also lists 2.85/3.00 mm and other spool sizes. The store only sells 1 kg at 1.75 mm, so only that is added.

## Values

| Field | Value | From |
|---|---|---|
| density | 1.22 | Product page + TDS |
| extruder_temp_range | 230–270 | Product page: 230–240 °C at 50–100 mm/s, 240–270 °C at 100–200 mm/s |
| extruder_temp | 250 | Tested on Bambu H2C |
| bed_temp_range / bed_temp | 70–80 / 70 | Product page |
| finish | matte | Product page ("Refined Matte Finish") |
| spool_weight | 189 g, plastic | **Measured** on an empty spool, see below |

**Spool weight:** I weighed an empty spool on a filament scale ([SpoolmanScale](https://github.com/Niko11111/SpoolmanScale)) and got 189 g. It's Sunlu's current **Gen3** spool, which is what PETG 2.0 ships on. Older (pre-Gen3) Sunlu spools weigh differently, so anyone with older stock should set the spool weight on the individual spool. *(Corrected from 180 g in the first commit, which was my mistake.)*

**Colors:** names and hex codes are from the "Color Code" table on the product page. Where the store and the product page spell a color differently, I used the product page's name (the store has "Oliver Green" for Olive Green and "Oak(Wood)" for Oak). The one exception is Klein Blue. It's `Blue (Klein Blue)`, to match the existing Sunlu PLA+ entry for the same color. The hex codes are lowercased to match the rest of the file.

**Name:** `2.0 {color_name}`, so the IDs don't collide with the existing Sunlu PETG `{color_name}` entry (e.g. `sunlu_petg_2.0black_1000_175_p` vs `sunlu_petg_black_1000_175_p`).

## Also in this PR: Wood name fix

`sunlu.json` fails the linter on `main`: the Wood line is named `{color_name} Wood` with material `WOOD`, so the name repeats the material. Because CI lints the whole file, any PR touching `sunlu.json` fails until this is fixed (this is also what's failing #485). I renamed it to `{color_name}`, as the linter suggests. Nothing else about those entries changed.

Side effect: those 4 IDs change (`sunlu_wood_cherrywood_…` → `sunlu_wood_cherry_…`), which is why the preview lists them as new. If you'd rather handle this differently, I'm happy to drop that hunk.

## Checks

`check-jsonschema`, `lint_filaments.py` (0 errors; the 11 warnings are all pre-existing entries), `compile_filaments.py` and `test_preview_catalog.py` all pass locally.

Every value was checked by hand against the linked sources. The data gathering and the JSON were done with help from Claude (an AI assistant). No values were generated.

title: Sunlu: add PLA+ 2.0 (20 colors)
body:
Adds Sunlu's PLA+ 2.0 line: 20 colors, 1 kg, 1.75 mm, plastic Gen3 spool.

I print mainly with Sunlu filament, so I'm reviewing the Sunlu entries here and adding or correcting them where needed. This PR adds a missing line. A separate PR will follow with corrections to the existing Sunlu entries.

## Sources

- **What's sold** (29 colors, 1 kg / 1.75 mm only): [Sunlu store, PLA+ 2.0](https://store.sunlu.com/products/moq-6kg-pla-2-0-upgraded-pla-pla-plus-3d-printer-filament-1kg)
- **Density, temperatures, hex codes:** [Sunlu PLA+ 2.0 product page](https://www.sunlu.com/products/pla-plus-2.0-3d-printing-filament). The "Parameter Information" and "Color Code" tables
- **Density and temperature cross-check:** [Sunlu PLA+ 2.0 TDS](https://media.sunlu.com/prod/20260327/81b1d361-0bd9-4783-ba0f-283a311c6870.pdf?filename=TDS), doc SL-TE-WI-081 rev A/1. 1.21 g/cm³ (ISO 1183); nozzle 205–245 °C; plate 50–60 °C

## Values

| Field | Value | From |
|---|---|---|
| density | 1.21 | Product page + TDS |
| extruder_temp_range | 205–245 | Product page + TDS: 205–215 °C at 50–100 mm/s, 215–245 °C at 100–200 mm/s |
| extruder_temp | 220 | Tested on Bambu H2C |
| bed_temp_range / bed_temp | 50–60 / 55 | Product page + TDS |
| spool_weight | 189 g, plastic | **Measured**, see below |

**Spool weight:** Sunlu now ships its filament on the [third-generation reusable spool](https://store.sunlu.com/blogs/products-review/sunlu-third-generation-reusable-spool-a-new-choice-for-eco-friendly-durable-and-efficient-filament-management) (launched 2025). I weighed an empty Gen3 spool from this line on a filament scale ([SpoolmanScale](https://github.com/Niko11111/SpoolmanScale)) and got **189 g**. It's the same spool and weight as Sunlu PETG 2.0 (#487). Older (pre-Gen3) Sunlu spools weigh differently, so anyone with older stock should set the spool weight on the individual spool in Spoolman.

**Colors:** the 20 colors with a hex code in the product page's "Color Code" table. Names follow the existing Sunlu entries (`Blue (Klein Blue)`), using the store's more specific name where it has one (`Ceramic White`, `Roasted Chestnut`). The hex codes are lowercased to match the rest of the file.

**Currently omitted:** the store also sells **Silver, Gold, Blue Grey, Lemon Yellow, Cherry Red, Mint Green, Chocolate, Orange and Grass Green** in PLA+ 2.0. Sunlu publishes no PLA+ 2.0 hex code for them, and I didn't want to copy codes from a different Sunlu line. I have asked Sunlu for the codes and will add these colors as soon as Sunlu provides them.

**Name:** `2.0 {color_name}`, so the IDs don't collide with the existing Sunlu PLA+ `{color_name}` entry (e.g. `sunlu_pla+_2.0black_1000_175_p` vs `sunlu_pla+_black_1000_175_p`). Same convention as PETG 2.0 in #487.

## Also in this PR: Wood name fix

The same one-line fix as in #487: the Wood line is renamed from `{color_name} Wood` to `{color_name}`, because the name repeats the material and the linter fails any PR that touches `sunlu.json`. The change is identical in both PRs, so they merge cleanly in either order. I've checked that #485, #487 and this PR merge with each other without conflicts. The 4 Wood IDs change (`sunlu_wood_cherrywood_…` → `sunlu_wood_cherry_…`), which is why the preview lists them as new.

## Checks

`check-jsonschema`, `lint_filaments.py` (0 errors; the 11 warnings are all pre-existing entries), `compile_filaments.py` and `test_preview_catalog.py` all pass locally. The local catalog preview shows 24 new entries (20 PLA+ 2.0 + 4 renamed Wood) and no near-duplicates.

Every value was checked by hand against the linked sources. The data gathering and the JSON were done with help from Claude (an AI assistant). No values were generated.

title: Sunlu: correct existing entries against Sunlu's official data
body:
I print mainly with Sunlu filament, so I've reviewed the existing Sunlu entries against Sunlu's official product pages and corrected them where they've drifted. New lines are in separate PRs: PETG 2.0 (#487) and PLA+ 2.0 (#490). No product or color is renamed here, so existing IDs are unchanged. The one exception is the Wood lint fix, which is shared with those PRs and explained below.

## Spool weights: Gen3 spool, 189 g

Sunlu now ships its filament on the [third-generation reusable spool](https://store.sunlu.com/blogs/products-review/sunlu-third-generation-reusable-spool-a-new-choice-for-eco-friendly-durable-and-efficient-filament-management) (launched 2025). This PR updates the empty spool weight of every Sunlu entry to **189 g**, the weight of the Gen3 spool.

- **Measured** on empty Gen3 spools with a filament scale ([SpoolmanScale](https://github.com/Niko11111/SpoolmanScale)): **PETG 2.0** (#487), **PLA+ 2.0** (#490) and **ASA** (this PR). All three came out at 189 g.
- **Not measured: PLA+, ABS, Silk TPU, Glow PLA, PLA, PETG, High Speed Matte PETG, High Speed PLA Marble, Wood and PLA Meta.** These are set to 189 g because they also ship on the Gen3 spool. I don't have them in stock yet, so I couldn't weigh them myself. I've asked Sunlu to confirm the Gen3 empty weight and which lines ship on it, and I'll update this if their answer differs.
- The previous values were 130 g on most lines, plus 162 g (PLA), 209 g (PETG) and 168 g (HS Matte PETG). These most likely describe older spool generations. **Anyone with older (pre-Gen3) stock should set the spool weight on the individual spool in Spoolman.**

## Data corrections

Each value is from the linked official product page: the "Parameter Information" table for density and temperatures, and the "Color Code" table for hex codes.

| Entry | Change | Source |
|---|---|---|
| PLA+ | density 1.24 → **1.21**. Hex: Green `5FC50D`→`1DAA27`, Yellow `F6FA00`→`FFF13F`, Cyan `39D0F1`→`00A3E0`, Beige `FFE8DB`→`F0E0D6`, Purple `942192`→`685BC7` (Sunlu: Lavender Purple; name kept) | [PLA+](https://www.sunlu.com/products/pla-plus-filament) |
| ABS | density 1.04 → **1.02**. Hex: Black `3A3C3B`→`000000`, Green `5FC50D`→`1DAA27` | [ABS](https://www.sunlu.com/products/abs-3d-printing-filament) |
| ASA | **added Sunny Orange** `ED7334` | [ASA](https://www.sunlu.com/products/asa-uv-resistant-filament) color table; sold on [Tmall](https://detail.tmall.com/item.htm?id=785576961176&skuId=6073725440909) (not currently listed on Sunlu's international store) |
| Silk TPU | density 1.24 → **1.21**. `bed_temp: 0` → `bed_temp_range [50, 60]`. Hex: Cream White `F7F1D1`→`F9F4E2`, Black `000000`→`1D1C1B`, Light Blue `92CECC`→`96E0E5`, Dark Blue `1D2353`→`304C87`, Burgundy `3F2028`→`66435A` | [Silk TPU](https://www.sunlu.com/products/silk-tpu-filament) |
| Glow PLA | density 1.26 → **1.23**. **White (Glow Green) and White (Glow Blue) had hex `000000`**, i.e. white filament listed as black. Now `DCEABE` and `F1F4ED` | [PLA Glow in the Dark](https://www.sunlu.com/products/glow-in-the-dark-pla-filament) |
| PETG | density 1.23 → **1.27**. `bed_temp` 80 → **70** (Sunlu: 60–70 °C; 70 tested on Bambu H2C), added `bed_temp_range [60, 70]`. Hex: Green `5FC50D`→`1DAA27`, Yellow `F6FA00`→`FFF13F`, Purple `942192`→`685BC7` | [PETG](https://www.sunlu.com/products/petg-3d-printing-filament) |
| High Speed Matte PETG | density 1.26 → **1.28** | [HS Matte PETG](https://www.sunlu.com/products/high-speed-matte-petg-filament) |
| High Speed PLA Marble | density 1.25 → **1.26**. Added `"pattern": "marble"` | [HS PLA Marble](https://www.sunlu.com/products/high-speed-pla-marble-filament) |
| Wood | density 1.25 → **1.17**. Hex: Wood `cfaf94`→`997d73`, Cherry `6c4f4c`→`ac7575`, Maple `c7aa8d`→`e5bd8e`, Walnut `564e44`→`58473f` | [PLA Wood](https://www.sunlu.com/products/wood-pla-filament) |
| PLA Meta | density 1.22 → **1.21** | [PLA Meta](https://www.sunlu.com/products/pla-meta-filament) |

**Deliberately left out:**
- The PLA+, ABS and PETG Red/Blue/Grey hex codes and the Blue → Blue (Klein Blue) rename. #485 already covers them.
- The PLA+ Sunny Orange hex code (`FC743A` → `ED7334`). It sits on the line #485 appends its new colors after, so changing it here would make the two PRs conflict. I'll follow up once #485 is merged.
- Renames that would change IDs (e.g. the `High Speed Matte PETG - {color_name}` name, which repeats the material). Each would break existing users' links, so they're better discussed separately.

## Wood name fix

The same one-line fix as in #487 and #490: the Wood line is renamed from `{color_name} Wood` to `{color_name}`. The name repeats the material, and the linter fails any PR that touches `sunlu.json`. The change is identical in all three PRs, so they merge cleanly in any order. The 4 Wood IDs change (`sunlu_wood_cherrywood_…` → `sunlu_wood_cherry_…`), which is why the preview lists them as new, together with ASA Sunny Orange.

## Checks

- `check-jsonschema`, `lint_filaments.py` (0 errors; the 11 warnings are all pre-existing entries), `compile_filaments.py` and `test_preview_catalog.py` all pass locally.
- A field-by-field diff against `main` shows only the changes listed above.
- This branch merges cleanly with #485, #487, #490, #481 and #259.

Every value was checked by hand against the linked sources. The data gathering and the JSON were done with help from Claude (an AI assistant). No values were generated.

- **PLA Matte, Bone White and Oak;** all of **PLA Lite:** sold on Sunlu's Tmall store (linked).

**Temperatures:** only the ranges Sunlu publishes. The exceptions are **Silk PLA+ and Silk PLA+ 2.0: 230 °C nozzle / 55 °C bed, tested on a Bambu Lab H2C**, both inside Sunlu's ranges.

## Spool weight

Sunlu now ships its filament on the [third-generation reusable spool](https://store.sunlu.com/blogs/products-review/sunlu-third-generation-reusable-spool-a-new-choice-for-eco-friendly-durable-and-efficient-filament-management), which I measured at **189 g** on PETG 2.0 (#487), PLA+ 2.0 (#490), ASA (#491), PA6-CF, PC and PP 2.0. These lines are set to 189 g on the basis that they ship on the same Gen3 spool. **I don't have them in stock, so I couldn't weigh them.** I've asked Sunlu to confirm the Gen3 weight and which lines use it, and I'll update this if their answer differs. Anyone with older (pre-Gen3) stock should set the spool weight on the individual spool.

**Density warnings from the linter:** High Speed Matte PLA (1.36) and LW-PLA (0.84, a foaming lightweight PLA) are outside the usual PLA range. Both are Sunlu's published values (product page and TDS linked above).

## Wood name fix

The same one-line Wood fix as in #487, #490 and #491 (`{color_name} Wood` → `{color_name}`), so `sunlu.json` passes the linter. It's identical in all of them, so they merge cleanly in any order.

**23 colors** in total; all hex codes are from the official "Color Code" tables.

**Material naming:** fiber-filled filaments use the `-CF` / `-GF` material convention from CONTRIBUTING (`PA6-CF`, `PA6-GF`, `PA12-CF`, `ABS-GF`, `PETG-CF`, `PLA-CF`), plus `fill`. ABS-FR is `ABS` with `FR {color_name}`, because FR isn't a fiber additive. PC-ABS is `PC+ABS`.

**Temperatures:** only the ranges Sunlu publishes. The exception is **PP 2.0**: nozzle **240 °C**, which I use. Sunlu publishes a single bed temperature of **40 °C**, and Bambu Lab's PP profile uses **55 °C**, which is what I print at. So `bed_temp` is 55 and `bed_temp_range` is 40–55: the low end is Sunlu's published value, the high end is Bambu Lab's.

**Spool weight:** **measured 189 g** (Sunlu's Gen3 spool) on **PA6-CF, PC and PP 2.0**, which I have in stock.

**Density warnings from the linter:** PC+ABS (1.081) and ABS-FR (1.15) are outside the usual ranges. Both are Sunlu's published values (product page and TDS linked above).
